user: The history of Berlin, Germany.
assistant: Shortly after World War II, Berlin became the seat of the Allied Control Council, which was to govern Germany as a whole until a peace settlement was concluded. However, in 1948, the Soviet Union refused to participate in the quadripartite administration of Germany and drove the elected government of Berlin out of its seat in the Soviet sector, installing a communist regime in East Berlin. The Western Allies continued to exercise supreme authority in their sectors, but gradually turned over control and management of city affairs to the West Berlin Senate and the House of Representatives. The Allies and German authorities in West Germany and West Berlin never recognized the communist city regime in East Berlin or East German authority there. After the fall of the Berlin Wall in 1989, the Final Settlement Treaty ended Berlin's special status as a separate area under Four Power control, and Berlin became the capital of a unified Germany. Government offices moved progressively to Berlin, making it the formal seat of the federal government in 1999. Berlin also is one of the Federal Republic 's 16 Länder. The Russian withdrawal from the territory of the former East Germany was completed on 31 August 1994, and ceremonies were held on 8 September 1994 to mark the final departure of Western Allied troops from Berlin.
[The End of Previous Conversation]

[The Start of Current Turn Question]
Why was the Berlin wall built?
[The End of Current Turn Question]

[The Start of Reference Answer]
The Berlin Wall was built in 1961 by the German Democratic Republic (East Germany) to separate West Berlin from East Berlin and the rest of East Germany. Its purpose was to prevent the large-scale emigration and defection to the West that had been taking place through the open border between East and West Berlin. The construction of the Wall was a response to the significant number of people leaving East Germany for the perceived greater freedoms and economic opportunities in the West. It became a symbol of the division between the Communist Eastern Bloc and the democratic Western world during the Cold War. During this period over 100,000 people attempted to escape and over 5,000 people succeeded in escaping over the Wall , with an estimated death toll ranging from 136 to more than 200 in and around Berlin .
[The End of Reference Answer]

[The Start of Assistant's Answer]
The Berlin Wall was built by the East German government in 1961 to prevent citizens of East Germany from emigrating or fleeing to West Berlin. Before its construction, about 3.5 million East Germans had circumvented emigration restrictions, many by crossing from East Berlin into West Berlin. The government officially described the Wall as an “anti-fascist protective rampart” meant to deter aggression from the West and claimed it was needed because of Western agents and West Berliners buying subsidized goods in East Berlin. However, these explanations were widely met with skepticism. [S1] [S2] [S3]
[The End of Assistant's Answer]

[The Start of Document]
Berlin Wall
The East German government claimed that the Wall was an `` anti-fascist protective rampart '' ( German : `` antifaschistischer Schutzwall '' ) intended to dissuade aggression from the West . Another official justification was the activities of Western agents in Eastern Europe . The Eastern German government also claimed that West Berliners were buying out state - subsidized goods in East Berlin . East Germans and others greeted such statements with skepticism , as most of the time , the border was only closed for citizens of East Germany traveling to the West , but not for residents of West Berlin travelling to the East . The construction of the Wall had caused considerable hardship to families divided by it . Most people believed that the Wall was mainly a means of preventing the citizens of East Germany from entering or fleeing to West Berlin .

Berlin Wall
The Berlin Wall ( German : Berliner Mauer , pronounced ( bɛʁˈliːnɐ ˈmaʊ̯ɐ ) ( listen ) ) was a guarded concrete barrier that physically and ideologically divided Berlin from 1961 to 1989 . Constructed by the German Democratic Republic ( GDR , East Germany ) , starting on 13 August 1961 , the Wall cut off ( by land ) West Berlin from virtually all of surrounding East Germany and East Berlin until government officials opened it in November 1989 . Its demolition officially began on 13 June 1990 and finished in 1992 .

Berlin Wall
Before the Wall 's erection , 3.5 million East Germans circumvented Eastern Bloc emigration restrictions and defected from the GDR , many by crossing over the border from East Berlin into West Berlin ; from there they could then travel to West Germany and to other Western European countries . Between 1961 and 1989 the Wall prevented almost all such emigration . During this period over 100,000 people attempted to escape and over 5,000 people succeeded in escaping over the Wall , with an estimated death toll ranging from 136 to more than 200 in and around Berlin .
[The End of Document]
